source_text:
τῆς ἐν νόμῳ. Hebr 7,3 Ἀπάτωρ, ἀμήτωρ, ἀγενεαλόγητος κατὰ τὸν τῆς ἱερωσύνης
λόγον, ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἐν τῇ φυλῇ τῇ Λευϊτικῇ ἐφαίνετο τίς τίνος ἦν ἱερέως ἢ γυναικὸς
ἱερείας. ἦσαν δὲ χρόνοι τῆς ἱερωσύνης, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐφημερίας εἶχον ἐνιαυσίους, οἱ δὲ
δι' ὅλης τῆς ζωῆς ἱεράτευον. καὶ ταῦτα εὑρίσκεται ἐκάτερα παρὰ τοῖς ἱερεῦσι τοῖς ἐν
νόμῳ, εἰ καὶ μὴ κατὰ τοὺς αὐτοὺς χρόνους. ἀπάτορα λέγει τὸν Μελχισεδὲκ καὶ
ἀμήτορα καὶ ἀγενεαλόγητον, μήτε ἀρχὴν ἔχοντα ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος κατὰ τὸν
τῆς ἱερατείας λόγον· οὔτε γὰρ γένος ἱερατικὸν εἶχεν, οὔτε ποθὲν ἤρξατο ὡς ἄλλον
διαδεξάμενος, οὔτε ἐξ ἐφημερίας ἕτερον, οὔτε ὡς νόμον ἔχων δι' ὅλης τῆς ζωῆς
εἶναι ἱερεύς. καὶ ὅλως πάντα τὰ λεγόμενα κατὰ παρεξέτασιν τῶν ἐν νόμῳ ἱερέων.
εἴρηται δὲ περὶ τοῦ Μελχισεδέκ· ἀφωμοιωμένος δὲ τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ θεοῦ, μένει ἱερεὺς εἰς
τὸ διηνεκές. καὶ πῶς ὁ Μελχισεδὲκ μένει ἱερεύς; ζήτημα τὸ λεγόμενον, ἔστι δὲ ἡ
λύσις αὕτη· ὥσπερ Μωϋσέα καλεῖ τὸν νόμον, οὕτω κἀνταῦθα Μελχισεδὲκ πῆ μὲν
τὸν ἄνθρωπον λέγει, πῆ δὲ αὐτὴν τὴν ἱερατείαν. εἰ τοίνυν ἀφωμοίωται ὁ
Μελχισεδὲκ διὰ τῆς ἱερατείας τῆς κατὰ Χριστόν, μένει διηνεκῶς· οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος
θνητὸς γάρ, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀξίωμα τῆς ἱερατείας. Hebr 9,11 Ὥσπερ ἡ σκηνὴ κατεσκευάσθη
ἐπὶ Μωϋσέως ὥστε τὰς λατρείας γίνεσθαι, οὕτω μείζων ἡ σκηνὴ αὕτη, τῆς χάριτος ἡ
σύστασις, τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ κεφαλὴν ἔχον τὸν Χριστόν. 351 Hebr 11, Πίστει περὶ
μελλόντων εὐλόγησεν Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακὼβ καὶ τὸν Ἠσαῦ. πρότερον ἔθηκεν τὸν Ἰακὼβ
εἶτα τὸν Ἠσαῦ, οὐ κατὰ τὴν τῆς γενέσεως ἀκολουθίαν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὴν τῆς εὐλογίας
τάξιν. Hebr 11,38 Ὧν οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος ὁ κόσμος. οὐ περὶ πάντων λέγει τοῦτο ἀλλὰ περὶ
τούτων τῶν τελευταίων οὓς καὶ μάρτυρας οἶδεν. ἐπιμέμνηται τῶν κλινάντων
παρεμβολὰς καὶ διὰ τὸ χρήσιμον τοῦ λαοῦ εἰληφότων χάριν. Hebr 12,1 Ὄγκον
ἀποθέμενοι πάντα. ὄγκος ἐστὶν ἡ ἁμαρτία τῆς κατὰ τὴν σάρκα ἀπολαύσεως, ἐξ ἧς ἡ
εὐπερίστατος ἁμαρτία τίκτεται. εὐπερίστατον δὲ εἶπε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τὴν εὐκόλως
ἡμᾶς περιϊσταμένην καὶ ἄγουσαν εἰς τὸ ἑαυτῆς θέλημα. Hebr 12,22–23 Πανήγυρις
γὰρ καὶ ἑορτὴ ἀγγέλων ἡ εἰς τὸν θεὸν δόξα, καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων
ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ κριτῇ θεῷ πάντων. Hebr 12,27 Τοῦτό ἐστιν ὃ λέγει
ὁ Παῦλος ἀλλαχοῦ· παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, ἵνα παρέλθῃ τὰ
πρόσκαιρα καὶ ἔλθῃ τὰ αἰώνια. Hebr 13,10–13 Τοῦτ' ἔστιν οἱ ἐν νόμῳ οὐκ ἔχουσι τὸ
δῶρον τοῦτο οὗ μετέχομεν ἡμεῖς. ἔξω δὲ τῆς παρεμβολῆς, ἀντὶ τοῦ ἔξω τῶν νομίμων
καὶ τῆς Ἰσραηλιτικῆς παρεμβολῆς.
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing the Hebrews 7:1-2 note] ... in the law.
Hebrews 7:3. Without father, without mother, without genealogy according to the account of priesthood, since in the Levitical tribe it was evident who was (son) of which priest or of which priestly woman. And there were times of priesthood: some had yearly courses of duty, others served as priests through the whole life. And both these are found among the priests in the law, even if not according to the same times. He calls Melchizedek fatherless and motherless and without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life according to the account of the priesthood; for he neither had a priestly family, nor did he begin from somewhere as having succeeded another, nor (succeeded) another from a course of duty, nor as having a law to be priest through the whole life. And altogether everything said is by comparison with the priests in the law. And it is said about Melchizedek: "made like the Son of God, he remains a priest continually." And how does Melchizedek remain a priest? The saying is a question, and the solution is this: just as he calls the law Moses, so here too by Melchizedek he means at one point the man, at another the priesthood itself. If, then, Melchizedek has been made like through the priesthood according to Christ, he remains continually; not the man, for (he was) mortal, but the dignity of the priesthood.
Hebrews 9:11. Just as the tent was built in the time of Moses so that the acts of worship might take place, so this tent is greater: the establishing of grace, the body of Christ having Christ as head.
Hebrews 11:(20) (label damaged). "By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come." He put Jacob first, then Esau, not according to the sequence of birth but according to the order of the blessing.
Hebrews 11:38. "Of whom the world was not worthy." He does not say this about all, but about these last ones, whom he also knows as martyrs. He also mentions those who turned back camps (armies) and who received grace for the usefulness of the people.
Hebrews 12:1. "Having put off every weight." The weight is the sin of the enjoyment according to the flesh, from which the easily-besetting sin is born. And he called "easily besetting" the sin that easily stands around us and leads (us) into its own will.
Hebrews 12:22-23. For the festal gathering and feast of angels is the glory (given) to God; "and to the assembly of firstborn enrolled in the heavens, and to God, judge of all."
Hebrews 12:27. This is what Paul says elsewhere: "for the form of this world passes away," so that the temporary things may pass and the eternal things may come.
Hebrews 13:10-13. That is, those in the law do not have this gift of which we partake. "And outside the camp," in place of: outside the legal ordinances and the Israelite camp.
pass_b_english: On Hebrews 7:3: “Without father, without mother, without genealogy” refers to the priesthood. In the tribe of Levi it was plain whose son each man was: which priest was his father and which priestly woman his mother. There were also set terms of priesthood: some priests served yearly courses of duty, others served as priests for their whole lives. Both kinds are found among the priests under the law, though not in the same periods. He calls Melchizedek fatherless, motherless and without genealogy, with neither beginning of days nor end of life, as far as the priesthood is concerned. He had no priestly family. He did not begin at some point as the successor of another, nor take over from another at the change of a course, nor did he have a law that made him priest for life. In short, everything said of him is said by comparison with the priests under the law. It is said of Melchizedek: “made like the Son of God, he remains a priest for ever.” How, then, does Melchizedek remain a priest? The statement raises a question, and this is the answer. Just as the law is called “Moses”, so here “Melchizedek” sometimes means the man and sometimes the priesthood itself. If, then, Melchizedek has been made like the Son through the priesthood that is according to Christ, he remains for ever: not the man, for he was mortal, but the dignity of the priesthood.
On Hebrews 9:11: The tent was built in Moses’ time so that worship could be offered in it. This tent is greater: it is the establishment of grace, the body of Christ, which has Christ for its head.
On Hebrews 11:20: “By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.” He put Jacob first and Esau second, not in the order of their birth, but in the order of the blessing.

On Hebrews 11:38: “Of whom the world was not worthy.” He does not say this of everyone, but of the last group, whom he also knows as martyrs. He also mentions those who “turned back armies” (Hebrews 11:34) and who received grace for the good of the people.

On Hebrews 12:1: “Laying aside every weight.” The weight is the sin of fleshly pleasure, and from it is born the sin that so easily besets us. He calls sin “easily besetting” because it readily surrounds us and draws us into doing its will.
On Hebrews 12:22–23: The glory given to God is the festal gathering and feast of the angels; “and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, the judge of all.”
On Hebrews 12:27: This is what Paul says elsewhere: “For the form of this world is passing away” (1 Corinthians 7:31). The temporary must pass, so that the eternal may come.
On Hebrews 13:10–13: That is, those under the law do not have this gift in which we share. “Outside the camp” means outside the ordinances of the law and the camp of Israel.

lemmas.gloss: without father, without mother, without genealogy (Hebrews 7:3)

choices.english: some priests served yearly courses of duty
choices.why: ἐνιαύσιος = yearly; old 'some had them for a day' misread ἐφημερία.
rejected: some had them for a day (old)

choices.term: τίς τίνος ἦν ἱερέως ἢ γυναικὸς ἱερείας
choices.english: whose son each man was: which priest was his father and which priestly woman his mother
choices.why: Explains 'without father, without mother'; old 'who was a priest or a woman priest' misread the genitives.
rejected: who was a priest or a woman priest (old)

choices.term: ἀπάτορα λέγει … κατὰ παρεξέτασιν τῶν ἐν νόμῳ ἱερέων
choices.why: Restates 'without father ... according to the account of the priesthood' but develops it (no priestly family, no succession, no law of life-long office); the edition marks no second form, so it is one note continuing, not a doublet.

choices.english: Just as the law is called “Moses”
choices.why: The subject of καλεῖ is unstated; rendered with a passive so that no subject is supplied (compare 'Moses is read', 2 Corinthians 3:15; not cited).
The edition's label is damaged (verse missing); the lemma is Hebrews 11:20, Isaac blessing Jacob and Esau.

choices.term: ἐπιμέμνηται τῶν κλινάντων παρεμβολὰς καὶ διὰ τὸ χρήσιμον τοῦ λαοῦ εἰληφότων χάριν
choices.english: He also mentions those who “turned back armies” (Hebrews 11:34) and who received grace for the good of the people.
choices.why: SOURCE_ISSUES item 4: old 'whom even a witness saw ... those who fell in the encampments ... because of the usefulness of the people having received them'. οὓς καὶ μάρτυρας οἶδεν = whom he also knows as martyrs; κλίνω παρεμβολάς is the phrase of Hebrews 11:34.
rejected: whom even a witness saw ... because of the usefulness of the people having received [them] (old)

choices.term: παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου
choices.why: Wording of 1 Corinthians 7:31; old English cited (Heb 12:27) for it.
